title: New Integrated Software for Soft X-ray Emission Spectrometer in EPMA System
content: The soft X-ray emission spectrometer (SXES), equipped with a varied-line-spacing grating as a spectroscopic element and back-thinned CCD camera for low-energy X-rays, is a type of electron-excited wavelength-dispersive spectrometer (WDS) for scanning electron microscopes (SEM) or electron probe microanalyzers (EPMA). It was launched by JEOL Ltd. in 2013 as a general product [1]. In addition to its higher energy resolution for low-energy characteristic X-rays, unlike conventional WDS systems with spectroscopic crystals, it does not require movement of the spectroscopic element or the detector. This allows simultaneous and reproducible detection of X-ray spectra across a range of X-ray energies, similar to energy-dispersive spectrometer (EDS) (Fig.1). Therefore, in addition to elemental analysis, SXES also provides the ability to determine the chemical bonding state of an element, and has come to be used in various research fields [1-5].
